  /workspace/LexicalAnalyzer/LexicalAnalysis.cpp   (lexer, complete)
  /workspace/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp            (LL(1) parser, complete)

  /workspace/agent_tests/test_parser_units.cpp     (unit tests: g++ -std=c++11 -Wall -o /tmp/pu agent_tests/test_parser_units.cpp && /tmp/pu)
  /workspace/LexicalAnalyzer/processed.txt and afterPreProcess.txt are GBK-encoded REFERENCE outputs from the original author — the lexer must reproduce them (modulo the UTF-8 vs GBK width of Chinese header text).

Grammars: test1 "E::=a|b|(T)  T::=EG  G::=,EG|@"   test2 "E::=AB|a  A::=C|bDA  B::=@  C::=cAD|@  D::=dBe"   test3 "E::=aH  H::=aMd|d  M::=Ab|@  A::=aM|e".
'@' = epsilon, '#' = end marker. Hidden grader tests compile and run the binaries and depend on these exact entry points (signatures must not drift):
  preProcess, mainProcess, IsIdentifier, IsNum, wtMatch, findError,
  load_file, split_into_rules, operator<<(rule), check_rules, check_set,
  operator<<(F_set), findFirst, checkFirst, findFollow, checkFollow,
  LL_1, operator<<(LL_1_table), print_state, syntacticAnalysis.

YOU MAY RUN the build/test commands above (read-only w.r.t. the repo: build into /tmp, never edit repo files, never run git write commands). Actually execute things — do not speculate. Report only defects you can demonstrate.


A prior auditor reported this finding:
{
  "title": "`@` inside a multi-symbol right part: FIRST treats it as epsilon but the parse loop pushes it as a literal stack symbol (wrong verdict in BOTH directions)",
  "file": "/workspace/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp",
  "line": 580,
  "severity": "major",
  "repro": "mkdir -p /tmp/x && printf 'S::=a@b\\n' > /tmp/x/test3.txt && g++ -std=c++11 -Wall -o /tmp/x/parser /workspace/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp && cd /tmp/x && printf 'ab\\n' | ./parser\n\nGrammar `S::=a@b` denotes S -> ab, so L(S) = {\"ab\"}.\n\nInput 'ab'  -> observed REJECT, expected ACCEPT. Trace:\n     #S      ab#   S::=a@b\n     #b@a    ab#   \"a\"匹配\n  栈顶终结符@与当前输入符号b不匹配，分析终止\n  字符串ab不是该文法的句子\n\nInput 'a@b' -> observed ACCEPT, expected REJECT (soundness break: '@' is matched as a real input terminal):\n  printf 'a@b\\n' | ./parser   =>  \"@\"匹配 ... 字符串a@b是该文法的句子\n\nThe program contradicts itself. firstOf() line 272-274 deliberately skips '@' anywhere in the string (`if (c == '@') continue; //\"@\"本身就代表空串，不影响它后面的符号`), and the printed table correctly shows [S,a] = S::=a@b. But syntacticAnalysis line 580 only special-cases the case where the ENTIRE right part equals \"@\" (`if (right != \"@\")`), so for \"a@b\" it pushes 'b','@','a' and the '@' later reaches the stack top and is compared as a terminal.",
  "fix": "In syntacticAnalysis, skip '@' while pushing instead of testing the whole string:\n\n    analysis_s.pop();\n    string right = rule_temp.right[0];\n    for (int i = (int)right.length() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n        if (right[i] != '@') analysis_s.push(right[i]);\n    }\n\nThis makes the push loop agree with firstOf()'s treatment of '@' and keeps the existing `X::=@` behaviour unchanged (the whole right part is skipped, nothing is pushed)."
}

You are a SKEPTIC. Try to REFUTE it: reproduce it yourself with the commands given. If it does not reproduce, or it is cosmetic/expected behaviour (e.g. UTF-8 vs GBK setw width, trailing spaces from setw padding, Chinese text alignment), mark isReal=false. Default to isReal=false when uncertain.

#!/bin/sh
# Build and run the LL(1) parser inside a scratch directory.
#
# Usage: agent_tests/run_parser.sh <grammar-file> <input-string> [scratch_dir]
#   e.g. agent_tests/run_parser.sh test3.txt aaabd
set -e
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
GRAMMAR=${1:-test3.txt}
INPUT=${2:-aaabd}
WORK=${3:-/tmp/parser_run}

rm -rf "$WORK"
mkdir -p "$WORK"
cp "$ROOT"/Parser/test*.txt "$WORK/"
# main() hard-codes ./test3.txt, so present the requested grammar under that name.
# (copying test3.txt onto itself is an error, so skip that case)
if [ "$GRAMMAR" != "test3.txt" ]; then
	cp "$WORK/$GRAMMAR" "$WORK/test3.txt"
fi
g++ -std=c++11 -Wall -o "$WORK/parser" "$ROOT/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp"

cd "$WORK"
printf '%s\n' "$INPUT" | ./parser
echo ""

content.text:
Reproduced both directions exactly as reported.

**Evidence (all commands actually run):**

1. `S::=a@b`, input `ab` → **rejected**, though the program's own table prints `[S,a] = S::=a@b` and `First(a@b)={a}`:
```
#S      ab#   S::=a@b
#b@a    ab#   "a"匹配
栈顶终结符@与当前输入符号b不匹配，分析终止
字符串ab不是该文法的句子
```

2. `S::=a@b`, input `a@b` → **accepted** (`"@"匹配` appears as a real terminal match), even though `split_into_rules` never put `@` in the terminal set (printed 提取终结符: `a  b`).

3. Minimal second case, `S::=@a`, input `a` → table prints `[S,a] = S::=@a`, `First(@a)={a}`, then the loop immediately fails: `栈顶终结符@与当前输入符号a不匹配`. The parser rejects a string its own generated table directs it to accept.

**The contradiction is internal to the program, not a convention dispute.** Two sites deliberately define `@` as epsilon *anywhere* in a right part:
- `/workspace/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp:216` — `if (c == '@') continue; //"@"代表空串ε，既不是终结符也不是非终结符`
- `/workspace/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp:296` — `if (c == '@') continue; //"@"本身就代表空串，不影响它后面的符号`

Only `/workspace/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp:604` (`if (right != "@")`) tests the *whole* string, so any embedded `@` gets pushed and later compared as a terminal. `/workspace/requirements/parser_analysis.yaml` does not mandate the whole-string form, so this isn't spec-sanctioned.

**Skeptical caveats I checked (they reduce severity but don't refute):**
- None of the three official grammars (`test1`/`test2`/`test3`) place `@` inside a multi-symbol right part, so `agent_tests/run_parser.sh test1/test2/test3` all behave correctly (`(a,b)` accepted, `bdeca` rejected, `aaebd` accepted), and `test_parser_units.cpp` passes 59/59. The `X::=@` path is unaffected (verified: `M::=@` expands correctly on input `aad`).
- So "major" is overstated — the bug is unreachable from the graded grammar set. But it is a demonstrable wrong-verdict-in-both-directions logic defect, not cosmetic/encoding-related, and the reported line, mechanism, and fix are all accurate.

input.reasoning:
Reproduced exactly, both directions, with the auditor's own commands. (1) Grammar `S::=a@b` with input `ab`: the program prints `First(a@b)={a}` and table entry `[S,a] = S::=a@b`, then the parse loop pushes 'b','@','a' and dies with `栈顶终结符@与当前输入符号b不匹配` -> `字符串ab不是该文法的句子`. (2) Same grammar with input `a@b`: accepted, with a literal `"@"匹配` step, even though split_into_rules explicitly excluded '@' from the terminal set (printed 提取终结符: a  b). (3) Independent minimal case I constructed, `S::=@a` on input `a`: table says `[S,a] = S::=@a`, loop immediately fails. So the program contradicts its own generated table.

This is not a convention dispute or garbage-in: the source deliberately defines '@' as epsilon anywhere in a right part at two sites — line 216 (`if (c == '@') continue; //"@"代表空串ε，既不是终结符也不是非终结符`) and line 296 in firstOf (`if (c == '@') continue;`) — while line 604 in syntacticAnalysis only tests the whole right part (`if (right != "@")`). /workspace/requirements/parser_analysis.yaml does not mandate the whole-string form, so the implementation is not spec-sanctioned. Nothing here is cosmetic/UTF-8/setw related.

Skeptical checks that survived: none of test1/test2/test3 place '@' inside a multi-symbol right part, so agent_tests/run_parser.sh on all three official grammars behaves correctly ((a,b) accepted, bdeca rejected, aaebd accepted), and agent_tests/test_parser_units.cpp passes 59 checks / 0 failures. The `X::=@` epsilon-only path is unaffected (verified via M::=@ on input aad). That makes the blast radius smaller than "major" suggests — it is unreachable from the graded grammar set — but the reported defect, its line, its mechanism and its proposed fix are all verified correct, so it is a real bug, just lower severity than claimed.
